headline: WHEAT DROPS 3.4%; WASDE CLOCK TICKING
subheadline: Chicago wheat had its biggest single-session drop in three weeks; corn and beans eased into the Labor Day weekend with the September WASDE seven days out.
lead: Chicago wheat fell 25 cents to $7.16 on Friday, the sharpest drop in the complex this session, with the FAO food price index rising on Black Sea logistics stress but the board pricing in something else: pre-holiday liquidation ahead of a WASDE that could reset everything. Corn gave back 3.5 cents. Beans slipped 14 cents. The funds are stepping out before a three-day weekend.
the_takeaway: Wheat's 25-cent drop is pre-WASDE fund liquidation; nothing changes until September 11.
teaser: Wheat fell hard into the weekend; the September WASDE on the 11th is the next real price setter.

one_number.unit: year-over-year rise in US beef export value, July
one_number.context: USDA trade data shows beef export value up 6% in July despite technical barriers to China. Pork fell on PRV headwinds. The beef number supports the cattle board's floor even as live cattle drift to $213.15.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn down toward $4.99; corn closed at $5.12, off just 3.5 cents, nowhere near the level.
yesterdays_call.note: Direction was right, magnitude was miles off; corn drifted but the harvest-pressure breakdown didn't materialize.

sections.title: WHEAT BREAKS INTO WEEKEND
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat tumbled 25 cents to **$7.16**, the session's biggest move in any grain, with FAO's August food price index rising on Middle East conflict and Black Sea logistics stress but the board ignoring the fundamental case and pricing pre-holiday fund exit instead.
- Oats ran 16 cents higher, a 4.7% move, on no clean catalyst, looks like position-squaring into the weekend after three straight down sessions.
- The next real information arrives September 11 at 11:00 AM CT; until then, wheat is a range defined by whoever comes back from the long weekend with a fresh view.
sections.catalyst: FAO Food Price Index rose in August on Black Sea trade logistics and Middle East conflict; board sold anyway.
sections.bottom_line: Pre-WASDE, pre-holiday liquidation. The fundamental case for wheat is intact; the fund case is not.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: yesterday's break deepened; two-day loss now tops 35 cents.

sections.title: GRAINS EASE; BEANS HOLD BETTER
sections.body:
- December corn slipped 3.5 cents to **$5.37**, four sessions in a row lower; harvest pressure is doing what harvest pressure does, and there is no fresh export sales number to interrupt it.
- November beans gave back a nickel to **$13.10**, still the strongest leg in the complex; the May 18 China purchase commitment (roughly $17 billion through 2028) has kept floor bids intact, but Friday offered no fresh buyer.
- Soybean meal held flat while soybean oil dropped 3.3%, widening the meal/oil spread -- protein demand is the engine, fat is the passenger.
sections.bottom_line: Corn is pricing harvest. Beans are pricing demand. They are not the same story and should not trade that way into the WASDE.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLD; BEEF EXPORTS SUPPORT FLOOR
sections.body:
- Live cattle slipped to **$213.15**, off 0.5%, with the Cargill multi-plant lockout (ongoing since May 19, still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity) keeping packer margins as the binding constraint, not cattle supply.
- Beef export value rose 6% in July year-over-year per USDA trade data, a number that argues the floor here is real even as cattle sit at the bottom 16% of their 52-week range.
- Trump signed new executive orders Friday aimed at supporting ranchers and expanding market access; separately, a House bill was introduced to nullify beef import authority, two political signals that the cattle producer has Washington's attention, for what that's worth at settlement.
sections.catalyst: Beef export value +6% in July (USDA); Trump executive orders on cattle market access signed Friday.
sections.bottom_line: Export data says the demand floor is real. The processing constraint is still the ceiling.

sections.title: ENERGY: DIESEL CRACKS DRIVE CRUDE
sections.body:
- WTI crude eased to **$91.22**, off less than a dollar, as Brent pushed toward $95 on record diesel crack spreads and tightening middle distillate supplies, not on crude fundamentals.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that has since cooled with the premium deflating again into August, is not the driver today; refined products are.
- Fall fieldwork diesel costs are the input story heading into harvest, not crude.
sections.catalyst: Record diesel crack spreads and tightening middle distillate supplies pushing Brent toward $95 (OilPrice.com).
sections.bottom_line: Crude is a sideshow. Diesel crack spreads are the harvest-cost number to watch.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA Piloting Satellites and Tech for Crop Yield Estimates
outside_the_pit.body: USDA Secretary Rollins confirmed Tuesday the agency is launching a pilot to replace survey-based acreage and yield estimates with satellite and remote-sensing data. For producers, this means future WASDE numbers could carry different error characteristics than the farmer-survey model built over decades.

outside_the_pit.title: Screwworm Port Reopening: CBP Now Active in Response
outside_the_pit.body: US Customs and Border Protection confirmed Friday it is facilitating sterile-fly movement and training personnel ahead of the phased reopening at Douglas, AZ set for August 24. The screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports remains the structural story under the historic feeder rally; the Aug 24 date is the next real tell.

weekly_thread.question: Will today's Crop Progress rating confirm the August yield cuts or add a weather premium back into corn and beans?
weekly_thread.status_text: The September WASDE on September 11 at 11:00 AM CT is the real resolution; Monday's Crop Progress set the table, but the board is waiting for the report.

the_more_you_know.title: The Diesel Crack Spread: What Farmers Actually Pay
the_more_you_know.body: Diesel rack prices track refining margins more than crude. With crack spreads at record levels heading into harvest, the per-gallon cost at the co-op is running well above what the WTI price alone implies. A $91 crude number is not a $91 farm input story right now.

watch_list.desc: Labor Day: all markets closed. No USDA Crop Progress published; next Crop Progress is Tuesday Sep 8 at 3:00 PM CT.
Weekly export sales: beans under 300K MT keeps the chart in charge; above 400K MT gives the November contract a bid back toward $13.20.
September WASDE: corn yield at or above 181 bu/acre would pressure December corn below $5.25; below 179 adds a weather premium back to the board.
Douglas, AZ phased feeder import reopening: watch the feeder/live ratio at or below 1.52 as returning Mexican supply begins testing the historic feeder premium.

daily_quote.text: Sell down to the sleeping point.
